title: GraphFlow fails to find next speaker when conditional edge is added (No available speakers found)
author: SogoKato

comments.author: salvprest
comments.body:
I have a similar problem,
i have the flow
A -> B -> C -> D
conditional:
D -> C  "OR"  D -> E
then
E -> C "OR"  E -> F

this give me the same error at the step B -> C of the linear flow (it don't see the C speaker)
if I Remove the conditional part of the flow, then the error disappear

Operating system:
Ubuntu 24.04
Python version:
3.12
Model:
gpt-4o

comments.author: ekzhu
comments.body:
Thanks for the issue. This will be addressed through #6542 

If a node's edges are all conditional, and none of the conditions are met, no next node can be found.

comments.author: SogoKato
comments.body:
Thank you for the response!

In the example above, agent D only has a single, unconditional edge to agent E, yet GraphFlow still fails to find that next node. This suggests that even non-conditional outgoing edges are ignored.

comments.author: Timilla
comments.body: Autogen's current graph-based approach is proving inefficient and is far behind what's achievable with LangGraph.

AI models will be writing most of the code for us in short future, so I don't see code writing as a bottleneck once we have agreed on design.

comments.author: ekzhu
comments.body: Can you make sure your conditional edges cover all possible outcomes from a node?

comments.author: peterychang
comments.body: The example by @SogoKato appears to have been fixed at some point between 0.5.7 and 0.6.1. @SogoKato or @Justin-12138 can either of you confirm whether this issue is present for you in autogen 0.6.1? 0.5.7 0.6.1 On a side note, the same bug that was the cause of https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/issues/6643 can be found in this code as well. `agent_e` is not being triggered because there are 2 parent nodes, only one of which may trigger. To resolve this, you can use `.add_node(agent_e, 'any')`. This is likely the underlying cause of the original issue as well.

comments.author: SogoKato
comments.body:
Thank you for looking into this, @ekzhu!

I can confirm that the original error is gone after upgrading from 0.5.7 to 0.6.1. In addition, as @peterychang pointed out, `agent_e` does not get triggered unless it is registered with `.add_node(agent_e, "any")`.
